evidence: Plaut. Trin. 4.4.21: hic ūnus, ut ego suspicor, servat fidem (Lewis & Short)
Ter. And. 1.5.46: ūnum hoc sciō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The plain word for “the only”: in quō ūnō acquiēscō, the only one I find rest in (Cic. Att. 9.10.1).

evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 41: fīlius ūnicus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: An only son or daughter is fīlius ūnicus, fīlia ūnica.

phrases.latin: nūper diē quārtō, ut recordor, et certē aquārium urceum ūnicum domī frēgit
phrases.english: the other day, four days ago as I remember, and I’m sure of it, he broke the only water jug in the house

phrases.latin: circumsiliēns modo hūc modo illūc ad sōlam dominam ūsque pīpiābat
phrases.english: hopping about, now here, now there, he kept chirping to his mistress alone

sources: Lewis & Short: unus · Lewis & Short: unicus · Lewis & Short: solus
